Synopsis:
Bank of Israel cut rates 25bps to 3.25% — third consecutive cut — with inflation at 1.5%, well below target midpoint. Deputy Governor Abir signaled further easing is data-dependent, contingent on inflation, shekel dynamics, and geopolitical developments. Terminal rate seen at 3.0% by mid-2027, with the next cut likely in November. Article explicitly notes Israel is diverging from the broader global trend of tighter monetary policy.
